decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - The proposed extensions to the side and rear of the roof due to their bulk, mass, disproportionate scale, and appearance, and limited sets ins of the side dormer feature and rear addition, would dominate the associated roof planes and have the appearance of unbalancing this pair of semi detached houses.  This would harm the character and appearance of the dwelling and the local street scene within the St Paul's Conservation Area.  It would therefore be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (All New Development), ENV-B.2.2 (Conservation Areas), H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations), and supplementary guidance for Residential Extension Guidelines, of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 2 - The proposed extensions to the side roof slope, roof due to their bulk, mass, and position, would be harmful to the living conditions to residents at 32 St Paul's Close by further reduction in sunlight and daylight, reduced outlook, and increasing the sense of enclosure and having an overbearing appearance. It would therefore be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (All New Development), H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations), and supplementary guidance for Residential Extension Guidelines, of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 3 - The proposed development would provide  insufficient off street parking in relation to the standards adopted by the Local Planning Authority, therefore giving rise to an increase in the demand for on street parking, interfering with the free flow and safety of traffic in the vicinity. It would therefore be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (All New Development), H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations), T.1.4 (Car and Cycle Parking and Servicing Facilities for Developments), and T.5.3 (Vehicle Crossovers and Hard standings) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.
description: Extensions to the side and rear roof slopes, installation of two rooflights on the front roof slope, and erection of a ground floor rear extension.
